hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? do you know why you were given your name?
options: then hold it close while you listen.
then this might make you curious. listen.
that’s a wish too, a brave one. listen.

steps.line: Five days after the prince was born, the king held a naming feast. Learned brahmins came to the palace, and eight were asked to read the baby’s marks.
Seven of them raised two fingers. “Two roads,” they said. “If he stays home, a great king. If he leaves home, a buddha.”

steps.q: The youngest, Kondanna, looks at the baby last. What does he say?
o: Two roads, the same as the others
One road: he will be a great king
One road: he will leave and become a buddha
steps.why: One finger, one road, and it led out of the palace. The king spent years trying to prove him wrong.

steps.line: The youngest, Kondanna, raised just one. “There is only one road for him,” he said. “He will leave home, and become a buddha.”

steps.q: You’re King Suddhodana. You want an heir, not a wandering monk. What do you do with Kondanna’s words?
o: Surround your son with comfort, far from sorrow
Send the boy to study with Kondanna
Ignore it, since seven others disagreed
steps.why: The texts say the king built him palaces of pleasure so he’d never see old age, sickness or death. It held until he was twenty-nine.

steps.line: They named the boy Siddhattha: the one whose aim succeeds. Siddha means accomplished. Attha means aim, or purpose.

steps.q: “The one whose aim succeeds.” Once he left home, how long did that aim take?
steps.why: He left at twenty-nine and woke up under the Bodhi tree around thirty-five, after years of teachers and hard fasting. Kondanna was with him through the fasting years.

steps.line: Remember the five friends in the deer park? The story says Kondanna was one of them, and years later, the very first to understand the Buddha’s teaching.

steps.q: When Kondanna understood the teaching, the Buddha added a word to his name. What did it mean?
steps.why: “Kondanna has understood!” the Buddha said, and from then on he was Añña-Kondañña: Kondanna who knows.

steps.line: Today, a parent whispers a newborn’s name for the first time. Every name carries a wish someone made for you.
steps.label: today

say: siddhattha is the pali form; siddhartha, the sanskrit form, is more familiar in english. gotama is his family name, and the sakyas are his people, which is why he’s later called sakyamuni, the sage of the sakyas.

traditions honor him by different names. theravada chants often call him bhagava, the blessed one. in japan, people may call him o-shaka-sama. in mahayana, he is one buddha among many, alongside amitabha, and maitreya who is still to come.

steps.q: Kondanna said “one road” at the naming, then waited some thirty-five years to hear the teaching. What does the story honor in him?
o: Being the cleverest reader of signs
His loyalty to the king’s family
steps.why: Seeing early isn’t enough. He left home to follow the prince, stayed through the hard years, and was ready when the teaching came.

today.say: today, say your own full name slowly, as if you’d never heard it before. who chose it, and what might they have hoped for you? hear the wish, without needing to agree with it. in many buddhist traditions, a teacher gives a new dharma name when someone takes refuge, as a wish too.
options: a small thing. it may surprise you.
many are. you can still hear the wish under it.
